headline: Approved $247,147.20 contract for Ledge Street Elementary playground and several special education service contracts, all 3-0.
summary: The committee approved a contract with M.E. O'Brien & Sons for a new Ledge Street Elementary playground, plus special education contracts with Beacon Communication Services, Reach the Top Tutoring, and Boothby Therapy Services. It also accepted the FY26 MM280 report of expenses over $10,000 and approved the FY27 August Transfer Report.
decisions: Approved the contract with M.E. O'Brien & Sons, Inc. of Medway, Massachusetts, for Ledge Street Elementary playground equipment and rubber surfacing for $247,147.20, 3-0.
Approved the contract with Beacon Communication Services for 1.0 SLP and 1.8 SLPA staffing for 2026-2027 at a cost not to exceed $368,943.75, 3-0.
Approved the contract with Reach the Top Tutoring for hourly tutoring services for 2026-2027 at a cost not to exceed $85,000.00, 3-0.
Approved the contract with Boothby Therapy Services for AAC and AT services for 2026-2027 at a cost not to exceed $44,640.00, 3-0.
Accepted the FY26 MM280 report of expenses over $10,000, 3-0.
Approved the FY27 August Transfer Report, 3-0.

FINANCE & OPERATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING 
MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 21, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Finance and Operations Committee was held at NHS North on Monday,  
September 21, 2026.  Ms. Lamphier called the meeting to order at 6:05 pm. 
 
Present:  Ms. Lamphier, Ms. Lewis, and Mr. Salvi 
 
Also Present:  Ms. De Gray, Mr. Smith, Mr. Beer, Ms. Mills (Ledge St.), and Ms. Gagne (Ledge St.) 
 
Also Present:  Members of the Public, Channel 22 Videographer 
 
Ledge Street Playground 
• Ms. Mills, Ms. Gagne, and Mr. Smith presented a new Ledge Street playground for 
approximately 450 students (pre-K through Grade 5), including 21% receiving special education 
services, more than 40% English language learners, and 73% economically disadvantaged. 
• Proposed site: former ball field on school district property with expanded space and accessible 
design. 
• The new site provides more space, improved accessibility, rubberized surfacing, safer separation 
from the roadway, fencing over approximately 75% of the area, lighting, better drainage 
(flooding) and a walking path. The existing playground will remain in use while future renovation 
decisions are considered. 
• Installation is expected to take about one month after equipment delivery, with weather 
potentially delaying surfacing until spring or summer.  
• Community fundraising: $25,000 for fencing, lighting, and a walking path; additional donation 
acceptance and spending details will be addressed through the district process. 
• City resolution R-26-048 authorized $247,386.18; the proposed contract is $247,147.20. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the contract with M.E. O’Brien & Sons, Inc. 
of Medway, Massachusetts, to provide the Ledge Street Elementary playground equipment and rubber 
surfacing in the amount of $247,147.20.  Funding is from account 91.1001.994600-081100-0000 
account (City Resolution R-26-048).  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Special Education Contracts 
 
Beacon Communication Services 
• Beacon Communications, a speech services company, have increased their rates modestly to 
$147.50 per hour for the SLP and $90 per hour for assistants. Staffing needs remain under review 
based on IEP service-hour data. 
• Questions were posed to Mr. Beer around the need to hire internally and reduce the number of 
contracted services. 
• Mr. Beer highlighted the systemic reduction in college students entering the field of education 
and special services as a global issue. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with Beacon Communication 
Services for staffing of 1.0 SLP and 1.8 SLPA for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed 
$368,943.75 Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  Motion 
passes 3-0.
FINANCE & OPERATIONS COMMITTEE MEETING  September 21, 2026 
2 
Reach the Top Tutoring 
• Reach the Top Tutoring: interim instruction for students between placements or hospitalized; 
maximum $85,000. 
• Mr. Salvi requested historical data on the number of students tutoring annually. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the contract with Reach the Top Tutoring for 
hourly tutoring services for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $85,000.00 Funding to be 
charged to the Operating Budget under Out-of-District Budget.  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Boothby Therapy Services 
• Boothby Therapy Services: augmentative communication and assistive technology; 288 hours at 
$155 per hour, maximum $44,640. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with Boothby Therapy Services 
for Alternative Augmentative Communication (AAC) and Assistive Technology (AT) contracted 
services for the 2026–2027 school year, at a cost not to exceed $44,640.00. Funding will be charged to 
the Operating Budget under Contract Services.  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Grant-Funded Contracts 
• A grant-funded behavioral therapist and BCBA supervision item was presented (informational).  
• Mr. Salvi requested information on the District’s spending for educating kids who need special 
education in charter schools or non-public schools.  
 
MS 280 – Purchases Over $10,000 
• Ms. De Gray explained the requirement for the District to present FY26 MM 280 expenses over 
$10,000. 
• The committee asked for the report to be given in Excel format and for a list of the account codes 
and the department they correspond to. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to accept the FY26 MM280 report of expenses over 
$10K.  Motion passes 3-0. 
 
Expenditure and Transfer Reports 
• FY27 August transfers were approved, including a transfer supporting English 3D digital 
licensing. 
• FY27 state adequacy aid is approximately $62 million, about $4.4 million lower than the prior 
comparison year, driven partly by lower enrollment and fewer free and reduced-price lunch 
applications. Heating, transportation encumbrances, grant funding, and expenditure trends were 
also discussed. 
• July and August expenditures, encumbrances, transportation, stipends, retirement payments, 
heating, and LED efficiency upgrades were reviewed. 
• Free and Reduced lunch application eligibility, income guidelines, outreach, and available 
support through schools and Meals Matters were discussed. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the FY27 August Transfer Report.  Motion 
passes 3-0. 
 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to adjourn at 7:31 pm.  Motion passes 3-0. 
  
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
